newsitem.title: GERMANY: German jobless record makes reforms vital - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: German jobless record makes reforms vital - Waigel.

text.p: Record post-war German joblessness in January makes radical reforms of Germany's tax and welfare systems more urgent than ever, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday.

"Record unemployment is the gravest problem facing the Federal Republic," Waigel said before a meeting of his Christian Social Union (CSU) party here. "Reforms of the tax and social security systems are thus even more necessary."
"The new jobless numbers compellingly show that we must act now," Waigel added, urging all parties -- including opposition, employers and trade unions -- to work constructively.
Waigel has put together a package of tax measures, agreed by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition, which would slash a net 30 billion marks in income and corporate taxes from 1999 onwards.
But Labour Minister Norbert Bluem's proposals for a reform of the German state pensions scheme is badly bogged down within Kohl's own Christian Democrat party (CDU).
